<!-- 1. Pre-compute axis_ranges of all relevant data -->
## 1. Pre-compute axis_ranges of all relevant data
```{python}
import pandas as pd
from dashboard_helpers import *     # contains helper functions, and lists of education_vars / health_vars
```

```{python}
# 1. Read data (cleaned data)
df = pd.read_csv(
    "data/panel_1980_2010.csv"
)

# 2. Compute axis ranges for all attributes (static; doesn't depend on UI input)
axis_ranges = compute_axis_ranges(
    df=df,
    x_vars=education_vars, 
    y_vars=health_vars,
)
```




## 2. Create sidebar controls
<!-- Begin sidebar -->
::: {.sidebar}      

<!-- Year slider -->
```{python}
ui.input_slider(
    "year", 
    "Year", 
    min=1980, 
    max=2019, 
    value=2000      # default value = 2000
)
```

<!-- Education metric (x) -->
```{python}
ui.input_select(
    "x_var",
    "Education Metric (x)",
    choices=education_vars,
    selected="secondary_enrollment"     # default value
)
```

<!-- Health metric (y) -->
```{python}
ui.input_select(
    "y_var",
    "Health Outcome (y)",
    choices=health_vars,
    selected="under5_mortality"     # default value
)
```

<!-- Region filter -->
```{python}
ui.input_checkbox_group(
    "regions",
    "Region",
    choices=[
        "East Asia",
        "Southeast Asia"
    ],
    selected=[
        "East Asia",
        "Southeast Asia"
    ]
)
```

<!-- Color-encoding toggle (by region / by income-level) -->
```{python}
ui.input_radio_buttons(
    "color_var",
    "Color Encoding",
    choices=[
        "region",
        "income"
    ],
    selected="region"
)
```

:::
<!-- Close (end) sidebar -->




## 3. Interactivity: Create reactive filtered data (i.e., data that is filtered dynamically based on the UI inputs' values)
```{python}
# Filter displayed-data dynamically, based on the UI inputs' values. (interactivity)

@reactive.calc  # when UI-input-values are changed, re-filter the displayed-data accordingly. 
def filtered():
    # invoke dashboard_helpers.filter_data(...) 
    #   a helper function in dashboard_helpers.py

    return filter_data(
        df,
        year=input.year(),
        include_east="East Asia" in input.regions(),
        include_southeast="Southeast Asia" in input.regions(),
    )

```




## 4. Render scatterplot using render_plotly
```{python}
from shinywidgets import render_plotly
```

```{python}
@render_plotly
def scatterplot():
    # What this does: auto-render the scatterplot on-the-fly, instead of using a fixed make_plot function. 
    fig = create_scatterplot(
        filtered(),     # filter for only records that match year and region
        input.x_var(),
        input.y_var(),
        input.color_var(),
        input.year(),
        axis_ranges,    # precomputed at the top of this file, q2.qmd
    )

    return fig          # NOTE: quarto auto-renders this!
```
